summary: In January 2158 at Sol, Riker and the new Bobs Charles and Arthur organize a rescue effort for the surviving human enclaves on Earth. Their two-week survey finds about fifteen million people scattered among almost forty marked locations. USE colony ships can carry ten thousand people in stasis, making the evacuation a fifteen-hundred-ship-or-trip problem, while HEAVEN vessels cannot land or enter an atmosphere. Scavenging autofactories are operating and a shipyard autofactory is hoped within two years; Riker shifts manufacturing toward transport, and Butterworth agrees that refugees may occupy his group's compound after its departure. Arthur begins outreach with manufactured communicators, but only about a quarter have been delivered or attempted and some groups resist contact.

updates.state: Cloud and dust obscure a heavily damaged surface; asteroid strikes and nuclear weapons have disrupted weather patterns, and dozens of impact sites are visible. A survey estimates that about fifteen million people remain, scattered among almost forty marked locations, and recovery is expected to take five to ten thousand years.

updates.description: A converted interplanetary freighter equipped as a Von Neumann probe. It is a small, light, resilient design intended to build copies of itself. It has a SURGE drive ring, fusion reactor, ramscoop generator, fabrication equipment including three large 3D printers, communications and sensor systems, and ROAMer and nanite systems; its autonomous cargo carriers move miners and materials; it has no weapons and little spare room. The version-2 HEAVEN design adds a larger reactor and drive, a rail-gun, ship-buster storage and launch facilities, higher-capacity replicant systems, room for ROAMers and mining drones, and greater cargo capacity. The HEAVEN project's communications are designed to send information from its vessels to Earth, not to support conversations across interstellar light-time delays. Version-2 HEAVEN vessels have better reactor shielding, and Riker's and Homer's versions are further strengthened. HEAVEN vessels are not designed to land or enter an atmosphere.

A planned USE colony ship designed by refugee scientists as an off-world refuge. Its plans require a space-based construction yard and a viable destination. It can carry ten thousand people at a time in stasis pods.
